method_family: Whole-brain T1 GM/WM radiomics signature (mRMR plus gradient-boosting selection, logistic Rad-score) combined with CDR and ADAS in a decision tree; same method family as P-512
what_it_shows: In an ADNI MCI sample split 7:3, the model combining radiomics, CDR and ADAS reached validation AUC 0.882. The whole-brain radiomics signature alone reached 0.784, CDR alone 0.632 and ADAS alone 0.695, and DeLong tests put the integrated model significantly above each (validation p = 0.0044, 0.0001, 0.0004). So adding clinical scales to the imaging-only model improves on it significantly. No multivariable clinical-only model (CDR + ADAS) was tested.

Moreover, the DeLong test showed that the diagnostic efficacy of the decision tree integrated model was significantly different when compared with the imaging histology label, CDR score and ADAS score, which suggested that the integrated model had superior performance to the individual predictors (Fig. 3; Table 4).
The AUCs of the training and validation set were 0.796 and 0.784, the specificities were 0.636 and 0.676, and the sensitivities were 0.865 and 0.863, respectively.

A total of 343 patients with MCI were selected from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database as study subjects. Among them, 154 patients progressed to AD during the 48-month follow-up. All subjects were randomly divided into a training set (n = 240) and a validation set (n = 103) in a 7:3 ratio according to enrollment time.
Among them, 154 converted to AD during the 3-year follow-up period.
